subject: Hiram Revels and Blanche K. Bruce
query: who was the first black senator from mississippi
title: Who was the first Black senator from Mississippi? Hiram Revels, 1870
answer: Hiram Revels was the first Black senator from Mississippi and the first African American to serve in Congress, sworn in on Feb. 25, 1870. The second was Blanche K. Bruce, who served a full term from 1875 to 1881. Both were chosen by the state legislature. Scott Colom, elected in 2026, will be the third.
body:
Revels, a Republican born to free Black parents in North Carolina in 1827, had been an alderman in Natchez before the Mississippi legislature picked him in January 1870 to fill one of the two seats left empty since Albert Brown and Jefferson Davis withdrew in 1861. Some senators objected that he had not been a citizen for the nine years the Constitution requires, citing the Dred Scott decision; his supporters answered that the 14th Amendment had overturned it. The Senate seated him by a vote of 48 to 8. His term was the short one and ended on March 3, 1871. He later led Alcorn College in Mississippi.

Blanche Kelso Bruce, born into slavery near Farmville, Virginia, on March 1, 1841, escaped at the start of the Civil War and later moved to Mississippi, where he held local posts including sheriff. The Republican-led legislature elected him in 1874, and he served from March 4, 1875, to March 3, 1881, making him the first Black senator to serve a full term. On Feb. 14, 1879, he became the first African American to preside over the Senate. After Reconstruction ended he lost his political base in Mississippi and stayed in Washington, where he served as Register of the Treasury. He died on March 17, 1898.

After Bruce left, no Black senator served anywhere in the country until Edward Brooke of Massachusetts took office in 1967. Revels and Bruce were chosen by legislators because senators were not elected by popular vote until the 17th Amendment (1913). That is why Democrat Scott Colom, who defeated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Nov. 3, 2026, election (the AP called the race on Nov. 11), will be the first Black senator elected directly by Mississippi voters. He is due to be sworn in when the new Congress convenes in January 2027.
in_the_news: Scott Colom's win in Mississippi's 2026 Senate race sent people looking up the state's only two earlier Black senators, both from the Reconstruction era.

faq.q: Who was the last Black senator from Mississippi?
faq.a: Blanche K. Bruce, who served from 1875 to 1881. Scott Colom will be the next when he takes office in January 2027.

faq.q: Who was the first Black U.S. senator?
faq.a: Hiram Revels of Mississippi, sworn in on Feb. 25, 1870.

faq.q: How many Black senators has Mississippi had?
faq.a: Two so far, Hiram Revels and Blanche K. Bruce. Scott Colom would be the third.

faq.q: Is Scott Colom the first Black senator from Mississippi?
faq.a: No. He will be the first elected by popular vote; Revels and Bruce were chosen by the state legislature in the 1870s.
